nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a field and let $(p_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be a formally orthogonal family of monic polynomials over $R$. Then there are sequences $(\alpha_n)_{n \ge 0}$ and $(\beta_n)_{n \ge 0}$ in $R$ with $\beta_n \ne 0$ for all $n \ge 1$ such that $p_0 = 1$, $p_1 = x - \alpha_0$, and $p_{n+1} = (x - \alpha_n) \, p_n - \beta_n \, p_{n-1}$ for all $n \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Favard's theorem, forward direction

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a field and let $(p_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be a family of monic polynomials in $R[x]$. Then $(p_n)$ is formally orthogonal if and only if there are sequences $(\alpha_n)_{n \ge 0}$ and $(\beta_n)_{n \ge 0}$ in $R$ with $\beta_n \ne 0$ for all $n \ge 1$ such that $p_0 = 1$, $p_1 = x - \alpha_0$, and $p_{n+1} = (x - \alpha_n) \, p_n - \beta_n \, p_{n-1}$ for all $n \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Favard's theorem

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a field. A family $(p_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of polynomials over $R$ is formally orthogonal if there is an $R$-linear functional $L \colon R[x] \to R$ such that each $p_n$ has degree $n$, $L(p_n p_m) = 0$ whenever $n \ne m$, and $L(p_n^2) \ne 0$ for every $n$.
nodes.title: Formally orthogonal polynomial family
